Subject: VaporAI pricing playback + token profile & peak TPS confirmation

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and two asks so we can put together a hosted pricing proposal that matches your load pattern. Short version: we want to confirm the monthly token range and the 99th-percentile peak TPS characteristics you mentioned on the call.

Recap from today's call:
- Product: VaporAI assistant (user-facing chat + batch summarization for enterprise customers).
- Current prod footprint: mostly chat, occasional batched jobs for nightly summarization.
- Rough monthly token window (your estimate): low 18M / typical 22M / high 25M tokens.
- Peak behavior: steady-state ~40 TPS, frequent short spikes up to ~420 TPS (10-20 minute windows) during traffic surges/feature launches; single-day stress tests can hit ~700 TPS for <5 minutes.
- Target unit economics: VaporAI is aiming for a baseline of $12-18 per 1M tokens for hosted inference to keep gross margins in line with current forecasting.

Two asks (so we can finalize scenarios):
1) Please confirm the monthly token range you'd like us to use for proposal (min / typical / max). If you have canonical monthly reports (billing or Prometheus token-counts) a log snippet or one exported CSV is perfect.
2) Confirm the 99th-percentile token TPS you want us to size for (is it 420 TPS as discussed, or should we use 700 TPS short-burst as the contingency for SLO planning?).

What we'll return by EOD Monday once you confirm:
- Hosted pricing scenarios (three slabs): conservative, expected, and launch-burst add-on pricing.
- Per-path unit econ table ($/1M tokens) with our recommended discounts for committed volumes.
- Latency/SLO impact matrix showing cost delta between keeping 99th TPS strictly under SLA vs allowing short-burst fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant.

Attached: a lightweight calc workbook (vaporai_token_calc.xlsx) showing our assumptions and a PDF with example hosted scenarios (redwood_hosted_pricing_scenarios.pdf). Also attached is the demo log we pulled yesterday (vaporai-demo-logs-20261209.jsonl) — redacted for PII.

Thanks — if you prefer, we can sketch two proposal PDFs (one optimized for $/1M and another for 99th-TPS headroom).

—
Stephanie Nguyen

Subject: Re: VaporAI pricing playback + token profile & peak TPS confirmation

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the crisp recap. A few clarifications and the numbers you asked for: 

1) Monthly tokens: our product analytics shows the following distribution over the last 3 months (approx):
   - Minimum month (seasonally quiet): 16.8M tokens
   - Typical month: 20.9M tokens
   - Peak month (marketing + big customer onboarding): 27.4M tokens
   We'd be comfortable using a 18M–25M band for pricing scenarios (that covers most months; highest months are episodic).

2) Peak TPS guidance: when we said 420 TPS we meant sustained spikes at the 99th percentile across 10–20 minute windows. For catastrophic short bursts during internal tests we've seen up to ~700 TPS but those are extremely short (<5 minutes) and we can schedule or rate-limit them. For SLA sizing please use 420 TPS (99th percentile) and include an optional burst add-on to cover 700 TPS short windows.

3) Unit economics: target $/1M tokens is $15 as a starting negotiation point. Prefer a slab that gives a visible step-down at 20M tokens/month.

4) Attachments: I'll DM the raw monthly token CSV and a 1-hour sample from Dec 03 showing the 420 TPS spike.

Next steps for us: please send the three pricing scenarios (conservative/expected/launch-burst) and a recommended SLA + fallback plan. If possible we prefer to see an example monthly invoice projection (line items) so our finance team can quickly compare.

Ethan
VP Product, VaporAI
ethan@vaporai.ai | +1 (212) 555-6789
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: VaporAI pricing playback + token profile & peak TPS confirmation

Forwarding Ethan's confirmation. Quick internal pricing sketch below so we have aligned options to send back. Attaching my scratch notes to the drive link.

Sketch assumptions (hosted API):
- Baseline slab (0-20M tokens): $16 / 1M tokens (includes autoscaling for steady-state up to 40 TPS)
- Commitment tier (20M-50M): $12 / 1M tokens (assumes 2–4 hr/day of burst headroom via autoscale)
- Enterprise burst add-on: $0.035 per token-second beyond committed headroom OR a dedicated burst pool option priced via monthly reserved capacity (estimate $9,000/mo to guarantee 700 TPS short-burst windows)

SLA/operational notes:
- For VaporAI's 99th percentile target of 420 TPS, recommend we size hosted path to handle 420 TPS at the committed tier (with warm autoscale).
- For the <5 minute 700 TPS test spikes, recommend fallback: route to a smaller quantized model (lower latency/cheaper) for burst coverage OR use an explicit One-Off burst seat (reserved capacity) priced above.

Action items for quote:
1) Produce three PDF scenarios: conservative ($18/1M), expected ($16 then $12 beyond 20M), and aggressive committed ($12 with 12-month commit + decreased burst cost).
2) Example invoice showing: token charges, burst add-on, request routing surcharge (if enabled), and 99th-percentile SLO uplift.
3) Ask product for a quick runbook on how fallback to quantized model affects response quality for VaporAI's summarization flows (we'll include expected quality delta in the proposal).

I'll turn the PDFs and invoice draft tonight and drop in the Drive link. If Vanessa has any changes to the per-1M numbers, flag them here.

—Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

2) By Monday AM: a one-pager on quality delta if we route bursts to a quantized model vs. paying for reserved burst capacity (so your product team can weigh cost vs. quality).
3) Please drop the CSV and the 1-hour sample in the Drive folder linked above (or send to me directly). Once we have the CSV we'll replace the workbook placeholders and give you a tailored per-month cost table.
